notes:
PPI checklist (2026-10-08) — BMW-experienced shop WITH A LIFT; cold start (seller not to warm it up); photos + a call with the tech.
1. Rear structure: battery box + tool tray out; diff-mount spot welds in the trunk floor; from below: subframe mounts, diff ears, subframe-to-body; cracks / old repairs / any reinforcement.
2. Cooling (no records in 26 yrs, long storage): pressure test; water pump play/weep; expansion tank, radiator necks, thermostat housing; fan clutch; coolant; any overheat history.
3. Front damage: lower lip torn; bumper support; radiator + A/C condenser behind it.
4. Gouged front wheel: balancer, check bend / crack near the spoke (seller says not cracked).
5. Identity: VIN [VIN] on windshield, door jamb, frame = the Arkansas title; LSD (diff tag or lift-and-turn test); engine is the original S52, unmodified.
6. CA smog: stored/pending codes, readiness monitors; original cats, stock exhaust.
7. Engine/drivetrain: VANOS rattle/codes; leaks (valve cover, oil filter housing, pan, rear main); clutch slip/engagement; gearbox/shifter; belts, pulleys, hose age.
8. Suspension/brakes: rear shock mounts (Z3 failure point); front control-arm + rear trailing-arm bushings; sway links; pads/rotors/fluid.
9. Body/top/interior: paint meter on every panel; rust (trunk battery area, floors — 16 yrs Arkansas); soft top + rear window + frame; window regulators; electrics/gauges; tire date codes.
Ask for: buy/don't-buy verdict; must-fix vs can-wait; rough cost for every finding.
TITLE (separate from the PPI): seller's name is not on the title (AR title -> donor parent -> school -> seller). Get photos of front+back of the title + donation + notarized purchase docs, and check with a CA registration service BEFORE paying anything.

2026-10-17: Jason's own mechanic (Mark) was sent the PPI repair list (power steering pump and hose, front struts, transmission output seal, cooling refresh with fan clutch, belts, tires and alignment, fluids, heater/A-C diagnosis; dealer quote $10,700) and declined the job outright: "That's crazy, no thank you." contradictions.detail: Listing title says 'Z3 3.0i Roadster' while the listing body says '2000 Z3M Roadster'. The VIN decode, Carfax (3.2 L) and PPI confirm an M Roadster.

PPI RO 19736 note 6 reads 'UNABLE TO OPEN TRUNK' and has no subframe or diff-mount line, yet the shop told the buyer verbally there were no issues with the trunk-floor welds. Both cannot describe a completed weld inspection.

Seller says the title 'was signed from I think original owner' to the donor. Carfax shows the original owner was in Alabama in 1999, followed by four estimated owners, with the last titled owner in Arkansas (2005 onward). The car has been serviced in Missouri and Seattle since 2021 with no new title ever recorded. The seller's account does not fit the recorded chain.

critical_evidence.evidence: Seller's trunk photos and video show a clean, rust-free floor with no lifted sealer at the left front corner and beside the tool tray. They do NOT show the differential-mount spot welds, the floor under the battery box or tray, or anything from below. The PPI sheet says 'unable to open trunk' and has no subframe line; the shop's 'welds fine' is verbal only. No reinforcement plates are seen.

Carfax has no reported cooling-system entry in 26 years, and the seller says 'no work I am aware of'. The PPI found discoloured coolant and a bad cooling fan clutch, with heater and radiator hoses green. No pressure test or water-pump check is recorded. No overheating was noted and the test drive was green.
2000 US M Roadster with the 3.2 L S52 (per VIN decode). The S54 rod-bearing issue applies only to 2001-2002 cars.

documentation.rationale: Identity is strong: the VIN matches across the decode, Carfax and PPI. The Carfax carries 17 dealer service lines and there is a written PPI. Missing: invoices, any cooling, VANOS or structure records, and title documents. The seller is not the titled owner and the chain since 2021 is unrecorded.

condition.rationale: The PPI lists multiple stated faults with no repair evidence: leaking front struts, P/S pump and line leaks, a transmission output-seal leak, bad fan clutch, discoloured coolant, low oil, cracked belt, no heat or air-distribution change, weak AC, aged tires. The front lip damage and wheel gouge are visible in photos. Offsetting positives: no engine oil leaks, good brakes, green steering and a green test drive.

price_value.rationale: $14,000 is well below the $16,659-$22,239 fair-value range. However, the PPI-quoted repair list ($10,700 at dealer rates), the bumper damage and the title-chain complexity absorb much of that discount.

mission_fit.rationale: A manual S52 M Roadster is the preferred future-keeper engine. It needs a meaningful catch-up and a title cleanup before it is a dependable keeper, which sits awkwardly with cash preservation.

logistics.rationale: The car is in Poulsbo, WA, far from Carmel. A PPI has already happened before any money moved, but it was at a seller-chosen general dealership. CA registration depends on an unrecorded, out-of-state title chain, and smog readiness is unchecked.

emotional_spec_fit.rationale: Genuine stock-appearing S52 manual M Roadster at 54k miles (the preferred engine). Silver over black is common, and the cosmetic damage to the lip and a wheel detracts.

what_would_change_verdict: Up: title documents showing a complete, signable chain that a CA DMV or registration service confirms it can register.
Up: specialist photos showing intact diff-mount welds from below, and a passing cooling pressure test.
Up: a price adjustment reflecting the PPI repair list at independent-shop rates.
Down: cracked or torn diff-mount welds, overheating or coolant loss on a pressure test, or a title chain CA cannot register.
evidence.mission_note: A manual S52 M Roadster is the right future-keeper specification, but this example needs a documented catch-up and a title cleanup first. That conflicts somewhat with the current cash-preservation strategy and is not a quick bridge.
evidence.rationale: The VIN, Carfax and PPI establish a genuine 2000 S52 manual M Roadster with consistent mileage (54,744), no reported title brands or accidents, and dealer service lines through 06/2024. The written PPI observes a substantial list of faults: leaking front struts, power-steering pump and line leaks, a transmission output-seal leak, a bad fan clutch, discoloured coolant, low oil, cracked belts, no heat or air-distribution change, weak AC and 5-6-year-old tires, quoted at $10,700 dealer rates. The lower front lip damage and a gouged wheel are visible in the photos. The rear structure, the key M-car weak point, remains open: the PPI says the trunk could not be opened, the verbal assurance about the welds is unsupported, and the seller's trunk photos omit the diff-mount welds. Cooling history is absent from the Carfax and the seller knows of no work. The title is not in the seller's name and no title has been recorded since Arkansas despite the car being in WA since 2021, so CA registration feasibility is unconfirmed. The $14,000 asking price sits below the fair-value range, before the documented repair list is accounted for.
evidence.next_action: Request photos of the Arkansas title (front and back) and every transfer document, and have a California registration service confirm the chain can be titled before arranging a specialist PPI of the rear structure and cooling system.
